rationale: The candidate is a coherent low-rise cultural mass with a readable dominant gesture: a compact bar-like enclosure wrapped around a carved central void. In all four views the same logic is legible, so it does not fail the cross-view coherence test. The thin blue access edge is answered by a real ground-level opening/void rather than a sealed frontage, which supports the public threshold requirement. The parcel is respected without simply filling the boundary. Programmatically, this can plausibly support a museum/gallery brief because it suggests a public court, controlled daylight, and a sequence around the void; however, the section remains somewhat generic and box-led rather than strongly gallery-specific. The mass is more successful as a carved, public cultural object than as a formally expressive section-driven museum, so program_fit passes but with only moderate section-program confidence.
